title: What the Civil Service Commission’s audits and decisions found about appointments
question: What have the Civil Service Commission’s inspections, audits and hearings, and the reports Human Resources makes to it, put in writing about how appointments are made?
finding: The Commission’s own audits of recruitments mostly found compliance, with two named lapses in verifying an appointee’s qualifications, one at the Department of Building Inspection and one in the Mayor’s Office. Requests for an inspection of merit-system practice rose from 55 in fiscal 2021-2022 to 112 in fiscal 2024-2025. Between 7 November 2022 and 2 February 2026 the Commission’s minutes record 52 agenda items on appeals of an examination or a rejected application: 41 denied, 6 put off to a later meeting, 5 granted in whole or part; appellants are counted, never named. Human Resources confirmed to the Commission that hiring someone as exempt first and examining afterwards was the standing practice where no eligible list existed.
how: The Commission’s annual report for fiscal 2020 to 2025 and two Human Resources reports heard by the Commission were read, and each row gives a one-sentence summary, a quotation of at most twelve words checked against the stored text, and the link recorded at download. The undated annual report is given the last day of the period on its cover. Appeal counts come from the table of 644 Commission actions built from the adopted minutes; an item heard at two meetings is counted twice. Outcomes are read from the wording of the action.
limits: The Commission’s records before November 2022 are not served, so earlier decisions are missing, and the table of actions has no rows after 2 February 2026 although later minutes are on disk, which looks like a gap in the table rather than in the Commission’s work. The audits cover a handful of recruitments a year and found most in order; the two lapses are about paperwork that could not be produced, not a finding that anyone was unqualified. Appeal items include continuances, so the number of separate appeals is smaller than the number of items. Individual inspection reports are not published; only the yearly counts are.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Department of Human Resources
rows.document: Report of Exempt Appointments, Position Requests, and Expired Appointments under Charter Sections 10.104-16 through 10.104-18
rows.said: Human Resources reported appointments in categories 17 and 18 that had run past their two- and three-year Charter limits although departments had been warned in advance.
rows.quote: “departments allowed appointments to continue beyond authorized limits”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Department of Human Resources
rows.said: Human Resources told the Commission that, where there was no eligible list, departments used to hire people as exempt pending a permanent appointment while the examination was held, and that since November 2022 they may fill such posts provisionally instead.
rows.quote: “hire ‘Category 16 exempt – pending Permanent Civil Service (PCS) appointment’”

rows.document: Annual Report, Fiscal Years 2020 to 2025: merit system audit, fiscal 2020-21
rows.said: The Commission’s audit of recruitments found that five of six departments had verified their appointees’ qualifications and that the Department of Building Inspection had not verified outside work experience for an employee appointed to class 6248.
rows.quote: “failed to obtain verification of external work experience for an employee”

rows.document: Annual Report, Fiscal Years 2020 to 2025: merit system audit, fiscal 2023-24
rows.said: Auditing exempt management appointments in nine departments, the Commission found that the Mayor’s Office held no documents verifying the education or experience of an appointee to a permanent exempt Deputy Director III post.
rows.quote: “did not possess the documents verifying the appointee’s education or qualifying work”

rows.document: Annual Report, Fiscal Years 2020 to 2025: Inspection Service
rows.said: The Commission received 55 requests for an inspection of merit-system practice in fiscal 2021-2022 (the report's own chart shows 65) and 112 in fiscal 2024-2025; in the latest year 32 concerned certification and selection, 7 appointments and 10 conflicts of interest.
rows.quote: “findings of significant merit system violations are scheduled for hearing”
